# Reported validation/read consistency race

GitHub: https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/issues/1383

An ordinary `pm comments` append can make an overlapping `pm ops validate --check-history-drift` report an item hash mismatch even though quiescent validation immediately before and after reports zero item hash mismatches.

Environment: globally installed `@unbrained/pm-cli` 2026.10.3, Linux, Node 25. The independent reproduction uses a minimal initialized workspace/global directory with no custom extensions. I copied 521 first-party item records and their history into that tracker to give the scan enough duration; the fixture has 522 items including its original seed.

Reproduction:

1. Initialize an isolated tracker with no extensions and enough ordinary items/history for validation to take several seconds.
2. Run `pm --json --output-budget unbounded ops validate --check-history-drift` to completion. The item-history counts are zero.
3. Start the same validation in the background. After 250 ms, append one valid comment to an existing item using a separate `pm comments <id> "concurrent validation reproduction"` process.
4. Await both commands. Run the same validation again without any writer.

Observed receipts:

| Validation | item hash mismatches | chain mismatches | version skews |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Before writer | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Overlapping writer | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| After writer | 0 | 0 | 0 |

The overlap identifies only the item receiving the normal comment. No repair or history mutation is needed between these reads. A small one-item fixture did not reproduce it reliably; the larger corpus did.

The copied fixture also has one constant, unrelated `_workspace` settings mismatch because its original settings differ from the copied source workspace history. That warning is present in all three reads. It is separate from the transient **item** hash mismatch described here. Neither source tracker nor item history is corrupted. No extension code or linked-test runner participates in the reproducer.

Expected: validation obtains a consistent item/history read, or detects that a writer advanced an item during the read and retries that item before asserting corruption. Genuine stable corruption must continue to fail strict validation.

Impact: strict CI/local tracker gates can report false corruption when another process is merely recording evidence. This was observed during an otherwise valid source-tracker quality run.

Duplicate search covered all issue states using `history drift concurrent`, `"hash_mismatches"`, `"validate" "race"`, `"history" "snapshot" "validation"`, and `"history" "concurrent" "validate"`. Existing merge-chain/conflict reports (#599/#606) describe concurrent writes or merges, rather than this read-versus-valid-write race. Linked-test workspace settings drift (#1109) is also a different path.


## Intake boundary

The reporter reproduction is retained as reported evidence. This delivery has not independently reproduced or repaired the race. It is queued and unclaimed; genuine stable corruption must remain a strict failure. The earlier closed authoritative-projection/cache fix pm-eax4y8 addresses ordering and stale caches, not a concurrent ordinary writer. Future verification also checks the replay/integrity invariant established by pm-hu11.
GH-1383: consistent SDK item/history drift reads during concurrent ordinary mutations

History drift validation can compare different item/history versions while a legitimate writer advances one item, reporting transient corruption although quiescent validation is clean. Preserve strict stable-corruption detection while observing a consistent read or bounded per-item retry.

Real isolated overlapping validation and comment append reproduces the old failure;Consistent-read or bounded retry eliminates false item mismatch;Genuine stable corruption remains a strict failure;Source and cache scans retain complete omission and integrity receipts
A concurrent ordinary item mutation does not produce a false corruption verdict; stable corrupted item/history pairs still fail strict validation.

Reporter on published 2026.10.3 and Node25 observed 0/1/0 item hash mismatches before/during/after one ordinary comment append in a 522-item disposable fixture, with chain and version-skew counts always zero. Source investigation is queued.

value.author: harness:codex
value.text: Investigation and TDD plan: source item documents are loaded before sequential history verification, so an ordinary writer can advance the stream after the document snapshot. Recheck only discrepant pairs against authoritative storage while holding the existing per-item writer lock; preserve strict corruption verdicts and bound contention. Retain core snapshot semantics for caller-provided documents and do not use history compaction. Regression owners are real SDK persistence and subprocess CLI transport, without test-only exports.
